analyst_view.overall: Early view: Everton under David Moyes are sixth with a tight defence and Thierno Barry on 10 league goals, and they have no European football, so they get a full week after their trip to Villa. Fulham under Alvaro Arbeloa play at Spurs on Thursday night, giving them less than three days' rest. That gap in recovery time favours Everton.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. I agree: Everton's league games have averaged 2.2 goals this season, and Fulham have scored only 10 in 10. Barry's form is the main reason it could go higher.

corners.text: The site has 10.1 corners. I lean higher: Everton attack mainly through crosses from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the full-backs, which brings corners, and Fulham like to keep the ball in the opposition half. Both sides should win their share.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I agree: neither side has a disciplinary problem in the news, and Moyes' Everton defend in an organised way rather than recklessly. James Tarkowski is the player most likely to be booked.

shots.text: The site has 26.4 shots. I lean slightly lower: Fulham's short turnaround from a Thursday game should take some energy out of their pressing, and Everton under Moyes prefer a few good chances to many. Mid-20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower: Fulham had most of the territory against Newcastle but finished poorly, and Everton's chances often come from headers that miss the target. Slightly fewer on target.
